newsitem.title: LATVIA: ENSKILDA SEES RIGA SHIPYARD AS OUTPERFORM.
newsitem.headline: ENSKILDA SEES RIGA SHIPYARD AS OUTPERFORM.

text.p: Swedish bank Enskilda said in a research report on Riga Shipyard that its shares were set to outperform the market and predicted net profits in 1997 of 1.5 million lats.

In a research note dated June 2, the Swedish bank said that the yard was experiencing strong earnings growth due to expansion in the handling of timber, where capacity should increase by 500 percent with no extra investments.
It gave outperform as its recommendation.

"We expect net profits of 1.5 million lats against 0.2 million lats in 1996," the bank said, noting the 1996 results contained a provision of 0.5 million lats as a Russian client went bankrupt. It said the full receivable was 1.5 million lats.
It noted that the Riga Shipyard was located in the busy and fast-growing port of Riga, was one of the largest yards in the Baltic and owned the region's largest floating dock.

"For 1998 we expect a growth in sales of three million lats, which is entirely due to expansion in the handling of timber. Net results are expected to increase by 400,000 lats, again attributable to the handling of timber," Enskilda added.
